summary: The Rhodes Scholarship for West Africa pays for postgraduate study at Oxford (fees, a stipend of £21,060 in 2026-27, visa, health surcharge and flights) for young citizens of 20 West African countries, including Nigeria and Ghana. It looks for top graduates (First Class or equivalent) with strong character, energy and leadership who want to serve others. The 2027 round closed on 27 August 2026; use this guide to prepare for the 2028 round, which usually opens around 1 June and closes in late August.
lookfor: Academic excellence (First Class Honours or equivalent)
Energy to use your talents to the full
Truth, courage, devotion to duty, sympathy for and protection of the weak, kindliness, unselfishness and fellowship
Moral force of character and instincts to lead
A clear, coherent two-year academic plan at Oxford
cycle: 2027 cohort: opened 1 June 2026, closed 27 August 2026 (references by 3 September); virtual preliminary interviews, then final in-person interviews in Abuja, Accra or Lagos in November 2026; outcomes in December. The 2028 round is expected to follow the same pattern from about June 2027 — check the new Information for Candidates.

eligibility.q: Are you a citizen of one of the 20 eligible West African countries (e.g. Nigeria, Ghana, Senegal, Sierra Leone, Côte d'Ivoire)?
eligibility.no: Check whether another Rhodes constituency covers your country, or consider Clarendon (no nationality limit).

eligibility.q: Have you lived in one or more of those countries for at least five of the last ten years?
eligibility.no: You are not eligible for this constituency. Check the constituency where you have lived.

eligibility.q: Will you meet the age rule for your round? (For the 2027 cohort: 18–24 on 1 October 2026; up to 25 for medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, law and engineering; under 27 for 'mature' candidates who finished their first degree on or after 1 October 2025.)
eligibility.no: The age rules are fixed. If you are over the limit, look at Clarendon, Weidenfeld-Hoffmann, Chevening or Commonwealth awards.

eligibility.q: Will you have a First Class degree (or equivalent) completed before the application deadline?
eligibility.no: Rhodes requires a First Class or equivalent. Consider Weidenfeld-Hoffmann or Chevening, which weigh experience more.

eligibility.q: Have you applied to Rhodes fewer than two times before?
eligibility.no: You may apply at most twice in total.

steps.title: Read the Information for Candidates
steps.why: Every rule (age, residence, documents, word limits, dates) is in this document, and the rules are strictly applied.
do: Open the West Africa page on the Rhodes House site.
Open 'Information for Candidates' and read it fully. When the 2028 version appears (around June 2027), read it again.
Write down your birth date and check the age window for your round.
Count your years of residence in West Africa over the last ten years.
tips: Save the National Secretary's email from the West Africa page for genuine eligibility questions only.
avoid: Relying on blog summaries of the age rule — use the official document.
check: I meet citizenship, residence, age and degree rules for my round.

steps.title: Understand what Rhodes selectors score
steps.why: Rhodes selects for character and leadership as much as grades. Your statements and referees must give evidence for each quality.
do: Open the Selection Criteria page.
Make a list of the four criteria: academic excellence; energy; character (truth, courage, devotion, kindness, unselfishness); leadership.
For each, write two true stories from your life where you showed it, with what changed as a result.
tips: Service that cost you something (time, risk, comfort) is stronger evidence than titles.
avoid: Listing positions held without showing what you did.
check: I have at least eight stories mapped to the criteria.

steps.title: Choose your two Oxford courses
steps.why: Your academic statement must show a clear two-year plan, and Scholars Elect make two Oxford applications. Changing course later is not normally possible.
do: Open 'Conditions of Tenure: courses covered' to see what Rhodes funds (PGCerts, PGDips and graduate-entry medicine are excluded; MBA/MPP get one year).
On Oxford's 'Find your course', shortlist courses that make up a two-year plan (e.g. two one-year master's, or an MPhil, or a DPhil).
Pick a first choice and a strong second choice.
For a DPhil, identify the area and 1–2 Oxford academics you would work with.
tips: Explain why each year/course is needed — the plan must hang together.
avoid: Picking courses with entry requirements you do not meet.
check: I have two named courses and can explain the two-year logic.

steps.title: Build your timeline and open the portal
steps.why: The window is short (June to late August). References are due about one week after you submit.
do: When applications open (about 1 June), go to the Rhodes applications page and create your account on the West Africa form.
Set dates: referees asked (-60), documents collected (-45), statements final (-10), submit (-5).
Read the Generative AI guidance: AI may help with editing and structure only, and you must disclose any AI use and confirm the statements are your own thinking.
tips: Submit a few days early so referees have time to upload.

steps.title: Prove citizenship and residence
steps.why: Applications without valid proof are rejected at the eligibility check.
do: Collect at least two of: certified birth certificate or affidavit; national ID (NIN slip/card); valid passport; voter's card; notarised citizenship affidavit.
Get evidence of residence for at least five of the last ten years (e.g. school or university letters, NYSC certificate, employment letters).
Get certified copies (e.g. at a High Court registry or by a notary) and English translations where needed.
Scan to clear PDFs.
tips: Use documents whose names match exactly; if names differ, add a sworn affidavit.
check: Two citizenship documents and residence proof scanned.

steps.title: Get transcripts, photo and CV details
steps.why: Official transcripts prove the First Class requirement; the CV is entered inside the form.
do: Request your official transcript from your university registry early; it must show grades and be in English.
Take a head-and-shoulders colour photo and save it as JPG.
Draft your CV entries offline: the form allows up to five entries per category (e.g. awards, leadership, service).
Choose your five strongest items per category.
tips: Ask the registry for a letter stating your class/rank if your transcript does not show it.
avoid: Filling the CV with minor items — five strong entries beat many weak ones.
check: Transcript, photo and CV text ready.

steps.title: Write the personal statement
steps.why: This is where selectors meet your character. It decides the longlist and shapes interview questions.
do: Read the three guiding questions in the Information for Candidates: which Rhodes quality you show most strongly; how past community work shapes what you will bring to Oxford; how you will address a pressing challenge from your context.
Choose one main thread (a problem you care about) and 2–3 stories that show it.
Structure: opening scene; what you did and why; what it taught you; how Oxford and the Rhodes community will grow it; your long-term commitment.
Weave the three questions into one story rather than three separate answers.
Get two honest readers; cut to 1,000 words or fewer.
tips: Be authentic — a Rhodes Scholar's advice is 'Be you'.
Show reflection: what you got wrong and how you changed.
avoid: Letting AI shape your story — only grammar help is acceptable.
check: It reads as one story; it is 1,000 words or fewer.

steps.prompt: Answer three guiding questions in one narrative: your strongest Rhodes quality; how past community engagement shapes your Oxford contribution; how you will address pressing challenges from your context.
steps.limit: 1,000 words (2027 cohort; check the current guidance)

steps.title: Write the academic statement
steps.why: Selectors must see a coherent two-year plan you are ready for.
do: Cover three things: your academic direction, motivation and long-term goals; your course plan (why each course is needed); your preparation and readiness.
Name both courses and, for a DPhil, your proposed area and possible supervisors.
Use specific evidence: projects, grades, research methods you know.
Cut to 450 words or fewer.
tips: Make sure it agrees with your personal statement — same purpose, different angle.
avoid: Vague goals such as 'to broaden my horizons'.
check: A reader can state my two-year plan in one sentence.
steps.prompt: Your academic direction, your two-year Oxford course plan, and your preparation for it.
steps.limit: 450 words (2027 cohort; check the current guidance)

steps.title: Secure 4–6 referees (at least 3 academic, 1 character)
steps.why: References give independent evidence of your intellect and character.
do: Choose at least three academic referees who can rank you (e.g. 'top 1%') and at least one character referee who has seen your service or leadership.
Ask them early; send your CV, both statement drafts, and the Referee Guidance document.
Enter their details in the portal; they receive an automatic email with an upload link.
Remind them: signed letter on headed paper, PDF, maximum two pages, by the reference deadline (one week after the application deadline in 2026).
tips: Pick referees who cover different parts of your life so letters do not repeat each other.
avoid: Friends, peers or relatives as referees.
check: All referees have the guidance and the deadline.

steps.title: Complete and submit the application
steps.why: Late or incomplete applications are not considered. There is no application fee.
do: Fill personal details exactly as on your passport.
Enter your CV entries, courses, referees and upload statements, transcript, photo and ID documents.
Proofread every section; check word counts.
Submit before 23:59 GMT on the deadline day (23:59 GMT is 00:59 the next morning in Nigeria and other WAT countries) and save the confirmation.
tips: Download a PDF copy of your submitted application to prepare for interviews.
avoid: Submitting at the last minute with poor internet.

links.t: Watch: How to Apply for the Rhodes Scholarship 2027 | Step-by-Step at University of Oxford (ScholarshipTab)

steps.title: Prepare for the virtual preliminary interview
steps.why: Up to about 70 longlisted candidates are interviewed online before the final shortlist.
do: Re-read your application and know every CV line.
Prepare 2-minute answers on: your motivation, your course plan, a time you failed, a current issue in your field and country.
Practise with a friend on video; test internet and power backup.
tips: Show openness to learning rather than claiming expertise.
check: I can discuss any part of my application confidently.

links.t: Watch: Acing Your Rhodes Scholarship Interview | Rhodes Scholars Share Their Advice (Rhodes Trust)

steps.title: Attend the final interview and social event
steps.why: Final interviews (30–45 minutes) are held in person in Abuja, Accra or Lagos in November; travel and accommodation are provided.
do: Confirm your attendance; locations are fixed and alternatives are not offered.
At the social event, be relaxed and genuine — no performance is required.
Expect deep questions on your character, choices and ideas; read widely on current affairs.
Bring originals of your ID documents if asked.
tips: Answer honestly when you do not know something, then reason aloud.
avoid: Treating the social event as a test to dominate.
check: I know my travel plan and interview date.

steps.title: If elected: apply to Oxford quickly
steps.why: The Scholarship is only confirmed when Oxford admits you, and some courses close in early December.
do: Apply to your two Oxford courses straight after selection, before their December or January deadlines.
Follow the Oxford graduate Application Guide for documents and references.
Meet all offer conditions, then apply for your UK Student visa (Rhodes covers visa fees and health surcharge).
tips: Prepare your Oxford statements in advance so you can submit within days of election.
avoid: Missing an early December course deadline.
check: Both Oxford applications submitted on time.

faq.a: No. The 2027 round closed on 27 August 2026. Prepare now for the round that usually opens around 1 June 2027.

faq.q: Do I apply to Oxford first?
faq.a: No. Apply to Rhodes first; if elected, you then apply to Oxford.

faq.q: Can I bring my spouse or children?
faq.a: The stipend is not meant to cover partners or dependants.

faq.q: How many times can I apply?
faq.a: At most twice, through one constituency per year.
